name: IGF-1 DES
lead: IGF-1 DES, written des(1-3)IGF-1, is a truncated form of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) that lacks the first three amino acids at the N-terminus. The truncation lowers its affinity for IGF binding proteins (IGFBPs), and in laboratory assays it was more potent than full-length IGF-1 at stimulating protein synthesis in rat muscle cells. [1][3]

It is a research peptide and has no approved human use. In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding forums, users discuss injecting it locally, for example into the chin, jaw or neck, with the aim of growing muscle or reshaping features: the proposed chain runs from local IGF signalling, to growth of the nearby muscle and soft tissue, to a fuller jaw, chin or neck line. [7][8][9]

IGF-1 itself is the main mediator of growth hormone's effects on muscle, cartilage and bone, and its synthetic form mecasermin is an approved prescription treatment for growth failure in children with severe IGF-1 deficiency. [12][13] Published work on the des(1-3) variant consists of cell-culture and animal studies; no published human study has tested it for muscle or facial appearance. [1][2][3][4][10][11]

paras: IGF-1 is a 70-amino-acid single-chain peptide that the liver makes mainly in response to growth hormone. It promotes growth in most cell types, especially muscle, cartilage and bone, and its production peaks during the pubertal growth spurt. [12]

Most circulating IGF-1 is bound to IGF binding proteins; one reference puts the bound share at about 98 percent, with IGFBP-3 the most abundant. The binding proteins extend how long IGFs persist in tissue, and individual binding proteins can either boost or dampen IGF signalling depending on the cell type. [14]

Des(1-3)IGF-1 is a naturally occurring truncated isoform that can also be made synthetically. Because it lacks the first three residues it is bound less by the binding proteins, so a larger share is free to act on the IGF-1 receptor. [4][3]

A 1989 study that synthesised IGF-1 variants truncated by one to five N-terminal residues measured protein synthesis in rat L6 myoblasts. The concentration giving a half-maximal response was 13 ng/ml for IGF-1 and 1.5 ng/ml for des-(1-3)-IGF-1, a roughly ninefold difference that the authors linked to the importance of the N-terminal region. [3] A companion review discussed why some molecular variants of the IGFs are more potent on protein metabolism, both by stimulating synthesis and by inhibiting breakdown. [6]
In bovine mammary cells grown in vitro, des-3-IGF-1 stimulated proliferation more than IGF-1 or IGF-2. [2]

In mice, an intraperitoneal injection of des-IGF-1 lowered plasma glucose by about half and increased phosphorylation of Akt-1 in skeletal and cardiac muscle, and of p70 S6 kinase in skeletal muscle but not cardiac muscle, a pattern that points to differing activation of growth pathways between tissues. [11]

Researchers have used des-IGF-1 as a tool to separate IGF actions from IGFBP effects, for instance in a rat brain-injury study that examined a role for binding proteins [1], and in rat hippocampal slices, where des-IGF-1 increased excitatory synaptic responses by about 40 percent through a postsynaptic mechanism. [10]

IGF signalling is involved in cell growth, differentiation and survival, and higher serum IGF is described as a risk factor for prostate and other cancers. [4] In a transgenic mouse model, expression of human IGF-1(des) in prostate epithelium was reported to cause hyperplastic prostate growth. [4] Wikipedia notes associations between high IGF-1 levels and cancer, and between acromegaly and colon and thyroid cancer. [12]

Another in vitro study reported that IGF-I has a dual effect on insulin release from rat pancreatic islets, and the mouse study above recorded a fall in blood glucose after injection. [5][11] Approved IGF-1 therapy has a defined, supervised medical role in severe deficiency. [13]
These are animal and laboratory findings; no human safety data for local injection of IGF-1 DES exist.

Mecasermin, a recombinant form of human IGF-1 sold as Increlex, is given by subcutaneous injection for long-term treatment of growth failure in children with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency, including Laron syndrome, where growth hormone does not work. It is prescription-only in the United States, Canada and Australia. [13][12]
Des(1-3)IGF-1 is not an approved medicine. Forum discussion of human injection of the peptide falls outside any approved use. [7][9]

On looksmax.org, IGF-1 DES appears in threads about local injection for chin, jaw and neck remodelling, in combination with growth hormone, and in stacks with topical androgens. [7][8][9] The discussion is mostly theoretical or anecdotal, and several replies in these threads are sceptical that it would help. [7][8]

In general terms, proponents point to the peptide's short-range activity and potency in cell assays as the reason it is considered for site-specific use; the same reasoning is applied to muscle in bodybuilding circles. [9]

No studies found. Related research on IGF-1 variants is confined to cell culture, rodent and bovine models. [1][2][3][4][10][11] Human trials exist for full-length IGF-1 as mecasermin in severe IGF-1 deficiency. [13]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, IGF-1 DES appears in threads about local injection for chin, jaw and neck remodelling, in combination with growth hormone, and in stacks with topical androgens [7][8][9].

claims.claim: Injecting IGF-1 DES locally can grow the chin, mandible and neck
claims.believers: Users say its local action and potency make it suited to targeting a specific area, and discuss using it for this purpose. [9]
claims.experts: No published studies have examined local injection of IGF-1 DES in humans; the available work is in cell and animal models [3][4].

claims.claim: Combining growth hormone with IGF-1 DES could help a teenager reach genetic height potential
claims.believers: A poster asked whether adding it to growth hormone would help reach genetic potential while growth plates are open, reflecting a belief that stacking raises effective IGF-1 [7].
claims.experts: No trials of IGF-1 DES for height exist. Replies in the same thread were sceptical [7].

claims.claim: Transdermal androgens plus IGF-1 DES form an effective facial remodelling stack
claims.believers: The author of one thread argues that locally absorbed androgens bind receptors in the jawline and that IGF-1 DES would add to this; he acknowledges side effects such as acne and facial hair [8].
claims.experts: No studies have tested this combination for facial structure. A commenter in the thread noted that preventing bone breakdown differs from causing bone growth [8].

claims.claim: IGF-1 DES is more potent than regular IGF-1 because it escapes binding proteins
claims.believers: Users cite the reduced binding-protein affinity as the reason it is regarded as stronger and more local than IGF-1. [9]
claims.experts: Laboratory studies support higher potency in rat muscle cells and bovine cells; whether this carries over to injection in humans has not been tested. [2][3]

card.summary: A truncated IGF-1 analogue forum users inject locally for jaw and muscle growth; only cell and animal data exist.
card.note: No human studies; IGF signalling is linked to growth of prostate and other tissues in animal work.

quick.overview:
IGF-1 DES is a shortened version of IGF-1 that binds less to carrier proteins and was more potent than IGF-1 in rat muscle cell assays. Forum users discuss injecting it into the chin, jaw or neck to build tissue.

No human study has tested it for appearance; the research is in cells and animals.
quick.mechanism: It activates IGF-1 signalling with reduced interference from IGF binding proteins, which in lab studies increases its effect on protein synthesis and cell growth.
quick.risks: No human safety data exist. Animal work reported prostate overgrowth with IGF-1(des) expression, and IGF signalling is described as a cancer-risk factor when elevated. It has no approved human use.

angle.text: Forum users describe local injection as a way to add tissue at a chosen site, reasoning from the peptide's higher potency in cell assays. Laboratory studies show stronger growth signalling than full-length IGF-1 in cells and muscle tissue; its effect on human facial structure has not been studied. [3][11]
